assumptions_invoked: immediate full drawdown of 10000 at t=0
arrangement fee of 100 paid at t=0 (net proceeds 9900 or fee as t=0 outflow)
24 equal monthly repayments of 450 starting at t=1/12
iterations: net drawdown form preferred: 9900 = 450 * a where a = sum_{k=1..24} (1+X)^{-k/12}; trial X=0.08: monthly factor r=(1.08)^{1/12}≈1.006434, annuity factor (1-r^{-24})/(r-1)≈22.024, RHS≈9910.8; trial X=0.081: r≈1.00651, factor≈21.99, RHS≈9895.5; trial X=0.0805: interpolate ≈9903; converge X≈0.0803 → 8.0% after rounding to 1 dp

assumptions_invoked: Part II (d) overdraft: total amount of credit deemed drawn down in full and for the whole duration
borrowing rate 12% nominal p.a. charged monthly → monthly rate 1%
€25 monthly account fee charged each month
interest + fees paid at end of each month; principal repaid at end of 3 months
Part II (e)(i) open-end: credit provided for a period of 1 year from initial drawdown; final payment clears balance of capital, interest and charges
nominal 18% p.a. monthly compounding → monthly rate 1.5%
standard annuity repayment of principal + interest
freedom of drawdown → Part II (a): total amount of credit deemed drawn down immediately and in full at t=0
nominal rate 8% → interest = 5000*0.08 = 400 (or on financed amount)
broker fee 200 financed into the balance at t=0 → total amount advanced/owed becomes 5200
equation: 5000 = (5200 + 400)/(1+X)^1   (financed fee increases the repayment obligation; net amount received by consumer is still 5000)
iterations: repayment=5600; 5000=5600/(1+X) → 1+X=1.12 → X=0.12 exactly; no iteration needed beyond direct solve; convergence immediate

weakest_point: Case 2 cash-flow timing (whether interest and monthly fees are charged in arrears and whether principal is repaid only at the end of the assumed 3 months) is the most assumption-sensitive; small changes in intra-period convention move the APRC by several points
